channels.who_to_report: A named clinician who holds or held a Utah licence. It also takes complaints about unlicensed people practising as though they were licensed, which is worth knowing in an industry that leans on unlicensed staff.
channels.how: File through the online complaint service, or download the PDF form and mail it. Complete every section; write N/A where one does not apply.
channels.phone_note: Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm Mountain, except state holidays.
channels.mail: Utah Division of Professional Licensing, P.O. Box 146741, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-6741
channels.note: Complaints are not public record under Utah law. DOPL publishes the disciplinary actions that result, so you can check whether anything came of an earlier one.

channels.name: Utah Office of Licensing, Division of Licensing and Background Checks (DLBC)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and inspects the residential treatment programs, therapeutic schools and outdoor youth programs themselves. It sets the health and safety standards, inspects against them, and can require corrective action, impose civil money penalties, or act against the licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It regulates the program, not the individual therapist - that is DOPL - and it does not investigate the abuse allegation itself, which goes to DCFS.
channels.who_to_report: The facility: staffing levels, restraint and seclusion practice, conditions, supervision, anything that is a standards problem rather than one person's conduct.
channels.how: Contact the Office of Licensing directly. Utah publishes its inspection findings, so it is worth reading what has already been cited before you call.
channels.phone_note: Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm, except state holidays.
channels.mail: Division of Licensing and Background Checks, 195 North 1950 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116

channels.name: Utah Division of Child and Family Services child abuse hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory intake point for child abuse and neglect in Utah. A report here starts a CPS investigation and can bring in law enforcement.
channels.who_to_report: A child currently at a program in Utah who is being abused or neglected, or who is in a situation likely to result in it.
channels.how: Call the 24/7 intake line, or use the online reporting form. Give names and ages, what happened, any injuries you saw, and dates.
channels.deadline: No deadline on making a report.
channels.note: Under Utah Code 80-2-601 anyone who believes a child is being abused must report it; failure to report can be a crime. Reporters acting in good faith are protected from civil and criminal liability. If DCFS itself mishandles the report, the independent Child Protection Ombudsman takes complaints about DCFS on 801-538-4589.

channels.name: Utah Attorney General, Medicaid Fraud and Patient Abuse Division
channels.what_it_can_do: Criminally investigates and prosecutes both Medicaid provider fraud and the abuse, neglect or exploitation of patients, where the abuse happened in a health care facility or any setting where a provider is paid by Medicaid. This is a prosecutor's office, not a licensing body: it is the channel that can put somebody in front of a criminal court.
channels.who_to_report: A program paid by Medicaid where a young person was abused, neglected or exploited, or where the billing does not match the care that was given.
channels.how: Call or email the division directly, or use the Attorney General's online report form.

channels.name: Utah Youth in Care (Congregate Care) Ombuds
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office inside DHHS for young people in residential programs, therapeutic schools and outdoor youth programs. It listens, advocates, conducts independent reviews, works directly with the program, and can open an investigation. It takes calls from a youth still inside a Utah program and from a parent in another state.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It does not investigate abuse or neglect allegations - those go to DCFS - and it does not investigate health and safety standards, which go to the Office of Licensing. It refers them on rather than dropping them. It does not give legal advice.
channels.who_to_report: A young person in a Utah program who feels unheard or unsafe, or a parent who cannot get a straight answer out of the program.
channels.how: Submit the online contact form. You will hear back within three business days, and contact is confidential.
channels.deadline: There is a time limit and the office states it two different ways: the programme page says you must make contact within 9 months of the incident, while the contact form says the situation must have occurred within the last 3 months. Treat 3 months as the safe assumption and call if you are outside it.

channels.name: Disability Law Center (Utah's Protection and Advocacy agency)
channels.what_it_can_do: Utah's federally mandated P&A. It investigates abuse and neglect in residential facilities, has a right of access to them, and provides free legal advocacy to eligible clients, including representation in hearings and court. Its published reports on Utah programs have forced state responses.
channels.who_to_report: A Utah program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis. Call and ask if you are not sure whether that applies.
channels.how: Intake by phone, or online through the site. It no longer takes walk-ins, though you can come in to fill in the paperwork.
channels.phone_note: Salt Lake City line 801-363-1347. Video Relay Service available.

states.note: Virginia is blunt about the cost of filing, and it is worth reading before you do. A complaint to the Department of Health Professions cannot be withdrawn once submitted, you cannot get a copy of your own form back afterwards, and Virginia law requires the details to be shared with the licensee you complained about. The Department cannot guarantee anonymity either - if you want to be anonymous, it warns that you must keep your identity out of the form and every document attached to it.

channels.name: Virginia Department of Health Professions, Enforcement Division
channels.what_it_can_do: Receives and investigates complaints for all thirteen of Virginia's licensing and regulatory boards, including the Board of Counseling, the Board of Social Work and the Board of Psychology, and the boards discipline the licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It has no authority to make a licensee return money or provide any other personal remedy. It cannot give you a copy of your complaint form once submitted, and the complaint cannot be withdrawn.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed counselor, social worker or psychologist in Virginia. Identify them by full name and licence type.
channels.how: Use the online complaint form, or return the Word or PDF form to the Enforcement Division by email, fax, post or in person.
channels.mail: Virginia Department of Health Professions, Enforcement Division, Perimeter Center, 9960 Mayland Drive, Suite 300, Henrico, VA 23233-1463
channels.note: Anonymity cannot be guaranteed. If you mean to file anonymously, the Department warns you must leave any identifying information out of both the form and every supporting document - naming yourself anywhere means you are not anonymous.

channels.name: Virginia Department of Social Services, Division of Licensing Programs
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and inspects children's residential facilities in Virginia and takes complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed children's residential facility. A facility providing behavioral health treatment may instead be licensed by the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services, which runs its own Office of Licensing.
channels.how: Use the online complaint form or call the licensing line.

channels.name: Virginia DBHDS Office of Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates behavioral health and developmental services providers in Virginia, including residential treatment programs, and investigates complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: A program licensed to provide mental health or substance use treatment, as distinct from a children's residential facility licensed by Social Services.
channels.how: Contact the Office of Licensing through its contact page, which lists the specialist for each region and service type.

channels.name: Virginia Child Protective Services Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour line for reporting suspected child abuse or neglect, which routes the report to the local department that investigates.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Virginia program.
channels.how: Call. Virginia says you do not have to give your name, and you do not have to provide evidence to make a report.

channels.name: disAbility Law Center of Virginia
channels.what_it_can_do: Virginia's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Virginia program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

states.note: Washington is unusually clear about what its health complaint system will and will not take on: unprofessional conduct, a provider unable to practise safely, and unlicensed practice, but not scheduling, personality conflicts or billing. It also has an independent Office of the Family and Children's Ombuds, which exists to look at how the state itself handled a child's case.

channels.name: Washington State Department of Health, Health Systems Quality Assurance
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines mental health counselors, marriage and family therapists, social workers and psychologists, and investigates three kinds of complaint: unprofessional conduct, a provider whose mental or physical condition means they cannot practise with reasonable skill and safety, and practice without a valid Washington credential.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It says plainly it may not be able to help with complaints unrelated to patient safety - scheduling problems, personality conflicts, disputes over bills or insurance.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed mental health professional in Washington, or somebody practising without a credential. Physicians go to the Washington Medical Commission instead.
channels.how: Use the Department's complaint forms. The complaint process page explains what happens to it afterwards.
channels.phone_note: Health Systems Quality Assurance customer service.

channels.name: Washington State Department of Health, facility complaints
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes and investigates complaints about the health care facilities the Department licenses, through a process separate from the one for individual providers.
channels.who_to_report: A DOH-licensed facility, including behavioral health agencies.
channels.how: Use the facility complaint process and the Department's complaint forms.

channels.name: Washington child abuse and neglect hotline (End Harm)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour line, which connects you to the local office that will take the report. It also takes concerns about a licensed facility, and about unlicensed care.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Washington program, and any concern about how a licensed facility is treating children.
channels.how: Call. A DCYF licensor starts acting on a referral within five working days, and a complaint is usually inspected and resolved within 45 days.
channels.phone_note: 1-866-END-HARM. 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
channels.note: For a complaint about DCYF itself rather than about a program, Constituent Relations takes those on 1-800-723-4831.

channels.name: Washington Office of the Family and Children's Ombuds
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office that reviews how the state's child protection and child welfare system handled a case, and publishes where it finds fault.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It examines the state's conduct rather than licensing or prosecuting a program.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person whose report to a Washington agency went nowhere.

channels.name: Disability Rights Washington
channels.what_it_can_do: Washington's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Washington program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.
